items.title: Blood clots are ‘incredibly common,’ even for pro athletes like Jalen Hurts. Here’s what to know.
items.content: Research has found that it can take more than six months for professional athletes to return to play after being treated for a deep-vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism.

items.title: Why smaller stocks face worse prospects than the S&P 500 in the coming years
items.content: The Value Line Median Appreciation Potential has a good record forecasting smaller stocks’ returns. And the next four years look bearish.

items.title: Strategist Tom Lee says he’s buying the AI-stock dip, and Cisco holds the key
items.content: Strategist Tom Lee says investors should not shrink from the pullback in stocks surrounding AI investment fears. He points to Cisco’s history as one reason to buy.

items.title: ‘I’m naturally skeptical’: I receive 10 calls a day offering me $15,000 loans at 8% interest. Is this a scam?

items.title: My unmarried partner of 17 years left me his $1.1 million home. His three children are livid. Should I share my inheritance?
items.content: “I never paid rent, although I put about $45,000 toward a new kitchen and a roof.”

items.title: South Korean IPO flop is the latest in a string of disappointments for the global AI trade
items.content: October alone has witnessed the shelving of three separate flotations planned for data-center providers, backed by AI powerhouses like Nvidia, Blackstone and SoftBank. Investors are not convinced of the sustainability of the capex outlay.

items.title: The multi-million dollar real estate portfolio of Buffalo Bills QB Josh Allen and actress Hailee Steinfeld
items.content: Josh Allen reached another milestone in his NFL career, but his life away from football is equally impressive—including the real estate portfolio he shares with his actress wife, Hailee Steinfeld.

items.title: It’s a rough housing market. Goldman Sachs expects it to get worse.
items.content: As bad as it is for the housing market — starts and transactions flat for the last three years with mortgage rates over 7% — it can still get worse.
